decisions.reference: Unmodified original A_FaceTarget, A_VileStart, A_StartFire, A_FireCrackle, A_Fire, A_VileTarget and A_VileAttack compiled as host C. Sight, damage, radius and angle boundaries are controlled. The spawn boundary explicitly normalizes the original repeated-x typo to target y. Fifty result/event fields match.
scope: All random starts, shadow-facing draws, spawn draws and ordered sound/damage events
Target-facing follow, unsigned angle wrap, target mass and vertical boost
Target/source/tracer identity and final fire placement
Actual open/closed portal sight and corrected x/y spawn while occluded
Cardinal target-facing follow, block relinking and sector/bounds refresh
Actual 20-point direct hit, 70-radius blast, vertical boost and boss blast immunity
Lost targets, missing or retired fire, inactive actors and stale generation handles
Sound/action callback failure before damage and during radius damage, including cleanup
Retargeting from sound and damage callbacks is observed before subsequent target use
Shadow-facing/spawn RNG and complete fresh-task heap cleanup
integration.controlledFailureSetup: Three exception/retarget fixtures assign the valid pain action to the player pain-entry state so an actual damage callback can be observed. The state action is restored after each fixture.

nativeDesign: Fire spawns at target x/y/z, correcting the original A_VileTarget x/x typo. The decision reference controls this spawn boundary; the real occluded-spawn case proves the correction.
Forced follow and blast placement refresh coordinates, sector bounds and block ownership through WorldActorPlace, as with revenant extra steps.
Attack targets are re-resolved by generation after sound and damage callbacks; missing or retired handles stop dependent work. Actor callbacks retain the existing deferred-reclamation requirement.
remaining: Boss actions and complete actor dispatcher
Persistent native game host, UI/audio, saves and progression
